outcomes: Application code emits one structured record to one or more interchangeable sinks
Request and event boundaries accumulate context fields without sharing mutable logger state
Trace and structured-error metadata remain machine-readable in JSON output
A panicking logged value cannot unwind the application call that attempted to log it
An operator changes a running service's log level through its configuration, never loses an error record, and sees how many records each level hides
nonGoals: Shipping, retaining, or querying logs in a remote service
Guaranteeing that arbitrary caller-owned objects are safe to marshal
Promising cross-runtime parity beyond the cases covered by the logging conformance corpus

requirements.text: Each sink write is panic-isolated so marshaling or formatting a hostile value cannot crash the logging caller.
Context-aware records apply field precedence in the order logger context, request FieldBag, call-site attributes, then framework-reserved fields.
Logger Flush and Close invoke every configured sink and return the first sink error they observe.
Every emitted record carries level, message, timestamp, logger name, attributes, optional context, optional trace identity, and optional structured error information.

text: The minimum level comes from the config key logger.level, one of debug, info, warn and error; without the key, LOG_LEVEL sets it, and otherwise it is info.
An unknown value counts as info.
SetLevel changes the minimum level of the default logger and of every logger derived from it, and the next record follows it.
Every logger.refreshSeconds, 30 by default and never when 0, a started application re-reads logger.level from its config files and CONFIG_DATA and applies a value that changed since the last read.

requirements.text: A record at error or above is emitted whatever the minimum level.
Every record a logger receives counts once in log.records, labeled with its level and the outcome emitted or dropped, the outcome dropped meaning the minimum level filtered it.

text: SetLevelLimit installs a process-wide limit that every logger consults on each record, without changing the live level: a record passes when it passes both its logger's level and the level the limit returns; nil removes the limit.
A record at error or above passes whatever the limit, and a record the limit filters counts as dropped.
